sections.h2: Who bills property tax in the city of Kalamazoo?
sections.html:
The City of Kalamazoo bills and collects property tax on city parcels through its City Treasurer, and the City Assessor's Office sets the values that bills are based on. The assessor works from City Hall at 241 W South Street, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and can be reached at (269) 337-8000 or assessor@kalamazoocity.org. Two drop boxes are available around the clock, one at the front of City Hall and a drive-up box on St. Johns Place at West Lovell Street.

Once a bill goes unpaid past the city's collection window, the Kalamazoo County Treasurer takes it over. That handoff is the point where sellers get surprised, because county charges are much heavier than city ones.

The city is the county seat of Kalamazoo County and, according to Wikipedia, had 73,598 residents in the 2020 census. It was first settled in 1829 as Bronson, took the name Kalamazoo in 1836, and is home to Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo College and Kalamazoo Valley Community College.

sections.h2: When are Kalamazoo property taxes due?
sections.html:
Summer bills are mailed by July 1 and due July 31, and winter bills are mailed by December 1 and due February 14 of the following year. A summer bill can be paid in one amount or in six monthly installments, with no interest if each one arrives on time. A winter bill has to be paid in full.

Kalamazoo city property tax calendar, from the City of Kalamazoo payment page and the county foreclosure timeline
DateWhat happens
By July 1Summer bills are mailed
July 31Summer bill or first installment due; a one time 3% penalty follows, then 1% interest on the first of each month
By December 1Winter bills are mailed
February 14Winter bill due in full
March 1Unpaid bills become delinquent and are paid to the County Treasurer

The city's card processor adds a 2.8 percent fee with a $1.50 minimum for credit or debit payments, and $0.85 for an electronic check. Paying by check at City Hall or the drop box avoids those add ons.

sections.h2: What happens if Kalamazoo property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After the local collection period, the County Treasurer adds a 4 percent administrative fee and 1 percent interest per month to the balance, plus fees for mailings, recording, title searches and site visits. The county's timeline shows the full path for taxes levied in 2025:

  • February 28 is the last day to pay the local treasurer; after that the balance is payable to the county.
  • On October 1 of the next year, a $15 notice charge is added.
  • On March 1 of the year after that, a parcel with taxes unpaid for over a year is forfeited to the County Treasurer, with 0.5 percent monthly interest, 6 percent retroactive interest and a $175 title search fee.
  • Recording of the forfeiture and redemption certificates adds $60, a site visit adds $50, and newspaper publication adds $50.
  • A bill unpaid for 25 months is foreclosed, and title passes to the County Treasurer on April 1.

The county says that once it takes ownership, there is no way to get the property back, although a person named on the deed may be able to claim excess auction proceeds. The treasurer cannot waive interest or penalties.

sections.h2: Can I get more time to pay a Kalamazoo tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes, in several ways. Eligible owners can apply to defer the summer bill so it falls due with the winter bill. The household income for the preceding year must not exceed $40,000, and the applicant must be 62 or older, a surviving spouse of someone who was, paraplegic, hemiplegic or quadriplegic, an eligible veteran or service member or widow or widower, blind, or totally and permanently disabled. Applications go to the City Treasurer's Office by September 15. Winter bills cannot be deferred.

If a bill has reached the county, the Kalamazoo County Treasurer can sign an extension agreement, but only after an appointment with the foreclosure prevention team. The county expects a plan to cover two tax years every calendar year, and condemned or dangerous properties do not qualify. Call 269-384-8124 for an appointment.

Partial payments are accepted at the county, which slows the monthly interest. The county staff can also screen for the principal residence exemption, a poverty exemption and the disabled veterans exemption.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Kalamazoo assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the March Board of Review. State law, MCL 211.30, has the board meet on the second Monday in March, or on the Tuesday or Wednesday after if the city adopts that schedule. It sits for at least 12 hours that week, and at least 3 of those hours must fall after 6 p.m.

If the board agrees your value is wrong, it must correct the assessed and taxable value so the property is relatively just and proper. A written notice of the board's decision has to reach you no later than the first Monday in June, along with information about appealing further.

The next step is the Michigan Tax Tribunal, which hears residential property tax appeals through a Small Claims division and an Entire Tribunal division. Small Claims hearings are usually by phone and about 30 minutes long, and many owners represent themselves. The notice from the board of review states the final filing date, so read it as soon as it arrives.

sections.h2: Does a Kalamazoo home sale need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
Yes for warranty deeds. Properties in the city need two certificates, because the county treasurer will not issue its own until the city treasurer has issued one. The city certificate costs $10 and is handled at City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036. The county certificate costs $5 for up to 20 tax ID numbers. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that taxes are paid for the five years before the deed.

The seller also owes transfer tax at recording, at $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, with the price rounded up to the next $500. On the city's Census median value of $179,000 that is $1,539.40. Deeds are recorded at the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, where the recording fee is $30.

Unpaid current taxes are normally settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Get the payoff from whichever treasurer holds the bill, since the city and the county do not share the same balance record.

sections.h2: What exemption should a Kalamazoo homeowner know about?
sections.html:
The principal residence exemption removes part of the local school operating tax from a home you own and occupy as your principal residence. According to the city, you must own and occupy it by May 1 of the year and file the affidavit with the Assessor's Office.

Selling changes the filing. The seller rescinds the exemption with the assessor, and the buyer files a new affidavit. A homeowner who buys a new home can hold the exemption on the old one for up to three years, if the old house is unoccupied, for sale, not leased and not used for business. That form is due by May 1 after the exemption is claimed on the new home, and it must be re-filed each year by December 31 to run for up to two more years.

If you are selling the house you lived in, tell the closing agent when you moved out. Wrong exemption status on a sold house leads to corrected bills later.

sections.h2: What do Kalamazoo housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Kalamazoo has more renters than owners, which is rare among Michigan cities of its size. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists 72,683 residents in mid 2025 and 29,523 households. Only 42.3 percent of housing units are owner occupied.

  • Median value of an owner occupied home: $179,000.
  • Median gross rent: $1,078 a month.
  • Median household income: $52,272, with 24.9 percent of people in poverty.
  • Land area: 24.69 square miles, about 2,980 people per square mile.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree: 38.5 percent.

Landlords with tenants, inherited houses and homes with deferred repairs often carry tax balances. The city's property record lookup in BS&A Online shows tax history, payment dates and any amount due on a parcel, plus permit history, so check it before you list.

faqs.q: When is the winter property tax due in Kalamazoo?
faqs.a: It is due February 14 of the year after it is billed, and a winter bill has to be paid in full. Unpaid winter and summer bills become delinquent on March 1 and move to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I pay Kalamazoo summer taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. You can pay the summer bill in six monthly payments by paying the first installment by July 31. If the first payment is late, a one time 3 percent penalty applies and interest of 1 percent is charged on the first of each month.

faqs.q: Who sets the assessed value of a house in Kalamazoo?
faqs.a: The City Assessor's Office does. If you disagree, the March Board of Review is the first place to appeal, followed by the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

faqs.q: Who qualifies to defer Kalamazoo summer taxes?
faqs.a: Owners with household income of $40,000 or less in the prior year who are 62 or older, disabled, blind, or an eligible veteran, service member, widow or widower. Applications are due September 15 to the City Treasurer.

faqs.q: What does a Kalamazoo tax certificate cost?
faqs.a: The city certificate costs $10 and the county certificate costs $5 for up to 20 tax ID numbers. Both are needed for a warranty deed on a property inside the city.
